item.title: Banbif proyecta que su utilidad escalará hasta en dos cifras gracias a la IA
item.description: “Manejamos las iniciativas de IA y todas las de innovación bajo una suerte de funnel en donde creemos que originaremos muchas y madurarán solo algunas, y creemos que en función al valor estimado de cada una de estas hay un múltiplo no menor de dos cifras de la utilidad del banco acá el 2030 que se proyecta como producto del rendimiento de estas nuevas soluciones”, confirmó a iupana Sergio Rospigliosi, gerente de innovación y desarrollo empresarial de Banbif. Banbif está trabajando en un ambicioso plan para desarrollar nuevos canales de experiencia digital y líneas de negocio basados en inteligencia artificial (IA) y así aprovechar sus beneficios. La entidad aseguró que explora una baraja de productos y capacidades, pero que el desafío es priorizar aquellos casos de uso claves que le permitan consolidar su estrategia de banca relacional en el mercado peruano.

item.title: El Niño’s Promise of Quieter Hurricane Season May Not Guarantee Good News for Insurers
item.description: While historically that would be good news for property insurers, which in recent years have faced an average of $30 billion in insured losses each season, that is less and less the case, said insurance brokers, catastrophe modelers and analysts. government scientists said El Niño arrived in June, which was also the start of the Atlantic hurricane season. or insurers, the periodic El Niño climate phenomenon has traditionally lowered the risk of costly Atlantic hurricanes, but decades of population growth along coastal areas and rising property values are forcing them to rethink that assumption.

item.title: FCA and Bank appoint members to their Transaction and Post-trade Reporting Harmonisation Taskforce
item.description: The FCA and Bank of England (Bank) have appointed members to their Transaction and Post-trade Reporting Harmonisation Taskforce. The taskforce will inform our long-term approach to harmonising transaction and post-trade reporting requirements across UK Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation (UK MiFIR), UK European Market Infrastructure Regulation (UK EMIR) and UK Securities Financing Transactions Regulation (UK SFTR). The members of the Architecture working group are: The working groups are supported by the Transaction & Position Reporting Team at the FCA and the Financial Market Infrastructure Data Team at the Bank.

item.title: FCA secures majority of victims’ money back from convicted fraudster
item.description: Victims of convicted fraudster John Burford are set to recover the majority of the money they invested after the FCA obtained a confiscation order against him. Clawing back stolen money from fraudsters and returning it to victims sends a clear message that crime doesn’t pay.' If Mr Burford does not pay the confiscation order within 3 months, he faces a default prison sentence of up to 5 years. The confiscation proceedings form part of the FCA’s ongoing work to deprive criminals of the proceeds of their crimes and get money back for fraud victims.

item.title: Schneider Electric’s VC Arm: The AI Buildout Is Creating A New Industrial Investment Cycle
item.description: Schneider Electric has spent nearly two centuries adapting to successive industrial revolutions — evolving from a 19th century steel and heavy machinery company into a global leader in energy management and automation. Around 80% of the startups in its portfolio have some level of commercial relationship with a business unit of Schneider Electric. Now, through its $1 billion venture arm, SE Ventures , the company is betting that the next transformation will be driven by AI’s collision with the physical world, from data centers and power grids to robotics and industrial automation.

item.title: Guernsey Financial Services Commission supportive of tokenised ILS
item.description: In a recent feedback paper published by the Guernsey Financial Services Commission (GFSC) on tokenisation of assets regulations, the organisation has hailed its support for re/insurers using tokenised ILS contracts, in a move that is expected to drive further innovation within the digital finance space. Building on work delivered through the Commission’s Digital Finance Initiative, the paper outlines practical measures to foster innovation while strengthening Guernsey’s position as a trusted international finance centre. The Commission also explained that going forward it will work with the States of Guernsey to simplify and clarify parts of the legal and regulatory framework for digital finance businesses.

item.title: Tunis Re premiums increase 2.2% in H1’26
item.description: Tunis Re (Société Tunisienne de Réassurance), the national professional reinsurance company in Tunisia, has recorded a turnover of TND 126 million ($42.6 million) for the first half of 2026, a 2.2% increase compared to the same period the year prior. Tunis Re attributed the decline to stricter risk selection and the absence of major loss events during the period. Investment income generated as at June 30, 2026, amounted to TND 17.028 million ($5.8 million), representing an increase of 6.1% compared with the same period of the previous financial year.

item.title: Cinven and La Caisse acquire majority stake in Optio from PCP
item.description: Optio, an independent international specialty managing general agent (MGA), has announced that international private equity firm Cinven, together with global investment group La Caisse (formerly CDPQ), have agreed to jointly acquire a majority stake from Preservation Capital Partners (PCP). Deepak Soni, CEO, Optio Group, said: “We are delighted to welcome Cinven and La Caisse as our partners as we embark on the next chapter of the Optio story. We are confident that, together with our new shareholder group, we will continue to build on these foundations, pursuing our growth strategy and expanding our capabilities while preserving the entrepreneurial culture and specialist expertise that define our business.” Cinven and La Caisse each have deep experience in the specialty underwriting sub-sector.

item.title: S&P upgrades West P&I to A- financial strength rating
item.description: West P&I, a mutual marine insurer providing protection and indemnity (P&I) and other specialist insurance cover to the global shipping industry, has received an A- Financial Strength Rating from S&P Global Ratings, with the ratings agency assigning a stable outlook. The rating follows a sustained improvement in its underwriting performance, with the insurer reporting a combined ratio of 98.0% for the financial year ending 20 February 2026. In its assessment, Standard & Poor’s said West P&I has strengthened its operating performance in recent years, enabling it to outperform many of its International Group peers across several key measures.

item.title: Jury Awards 78-Year Old Victim $56 Million for Crash Caused by Amazon Delivery Driver
item.description: A Massachusetts jury has awarded $56 million to a 78-year old man who suffered catastrophic physical and brain injuries after his car was hit by an Amazon delivery van in 2024. Amazon had denied it was liable because the driver responsible for the accident was not an employer of Amazon directly but was instead an employee of Agora Logistics LLC, an Amazon independent delivery service partner and a co-defendant in the lawsuit. The head-on collision occurred on a New Hampshire road when the driver of an Amazon-branded delivery truck allegedly fell asleep at the wheel and crossed the center line and struck Carnwath’s vehicle.

item.title: Fire Aboard Floating Restaurant on New Hampshire Lake Under Investigation
item.description: New Hampshire officials ere investigating a fire on board The Dive, a floating bar and restaurant on Lake Winnipesaukee. The State Police Marine Patrol received reports of a fire on board The Dive, a floating bar and restaurant, which was anchored at the Smalls Cove sandbar and open for business at the time. While all aspects remain under investigation, at this time, investigators believe the fire started in the kitchen area.

item.title: People: Bowie Named CEO of Praxis Reciprocal Exchange
item.description: Tampa-based Praxis Reciprocal Exchange, approved to do business in Florida in September 2025, has named Ross Bowie chief executive officer, the company announced. As CEO, Bowie will lead underwriting, distribution, and strategy across the Praxis operating companies, working with President and CFO Jennifer Gravelle and the leadership team to build on the organization’s first-year momentum and grow the exchange and MGA, the company noted. Bowie comes to Praxis after two years as president, chief risk officer, then CEO of Private Client Select Insurance Services, a joint venture between AIG and Stone Point Capital that focuses on high-net-worth individuals.

item.title: Ominimo raises $22.5 million
item.description: Hungarian car insurance startup Ominimo announced a $22.5 million Series B funding round that values the company at $1.6 billion. Founded in 2024, the startup claims that it is approaching one million customers across four European markets. Ominimo partners with Signal Iduna in Hungary and DA Direkt, Zurich’s German unit, in Poland, the Netherlands and Sweden.

item.title: Tesla’s Cratering Cybertruck Sales Evoke Ford Edsel Comparisons
item.description: Edsel sales dropped each year the model was on the market, and Ford discontinued the car in 1959. Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck sales in its financial releases, and investors likely will be more focused on the company’s spending toward driverless vehicle and robotics ambitions when it reports second-quarter earnings on Wednesday. Tesla Inc.’s Cybertruck may well be on its way to claiming that title.

item.title: Computer Scientists: 2M Cars with Anti-Theft Systems Installed by Dealers at Higher Theft Risk
item.description: Newswise — At least 2.2 million cars on the road today are vulnerable to an attack that allows thieves to lock and unlock doors and immobilize vehicle engines remotely via a Bluetooth connection, computer scientists at the University of California San Diego have found. The vulnerability is due to a device controlled via a smartphone app that is typically installed by dealerships to manage vehicle inventory and prevent theft. When a dealership sells a vehicle, they market the device and app as a paid upgrade – an anti-theft tool as well as a tool to control the car via an app.

item.title: You don't need to pay to claim: FCA launches nationwide car finance campaign
item.description: Millions of car finance customers who may be owed compensation can get help making a complaint for free, as the FCA launches a national advertising campaign. Our free tools are there to help people feel claim confident – so they can get any money owed back without it costing them a penny.' Many car finance customers are already acting – 59% have made or are considering a claim – but a significant group (23%) say they are unsure of their options. Research by the FCA found that 27% of car finance customers lack confidence to make a complaint without using a claims management company (CMC) or law firm, despite free tools from the FCA being available.

item.title: UCITS catastrophe bond fund sector surpasses $21bn of assets for first time
item.description: Catastrophe bond funds in the UCITS format have now added more than $1.84 billion of assets through 2026 so far, with the sector surpassing the $21 billion milestone for the first time this month. That equates to nearly 10% growth in the combined assets of the UCITS catastrophe bond fund sector over the course of this year so far. In 2026 so far, UCITS cat bond fund assets reached the $20 billion milestone for the first time ever in February, but then declined slightly to around $19.8 billion by the end of Q1 2026.

item.title: Tokio Marine HCC names Megann Pfeffer President of Public Risk Group
item.description: Tokio Marine HCC (TMHCC), a Houston, Texas-headquartered specialty insurance company, has announced the appointment of Megann Pfeffer as President of its Public Risk Group, with the role taking effect immediately, reporting to Matt Overlan, Chief Executive Officer of Tokio Marine HCC – Specialty Group. Pfeffer joined the organisation in 2022 as Chief Operating Officer of the Public Risk Group. Pfeffer will now oversee the overall management and long-term strategy of the Public Risk Group, which provides insurance products for public sector organisations, including municipalities and special districts.

item.title: MS Transverse’s new E&S front Newhall gets A+ rating by AM Best
item.description: Credit ratings agency AM Best has assigned MS Transverse’s new excess and surplus (E&S) entity, Newhall Specialty Insurance Company (NSIC), a Financial Strength Rating of A+ (Superior) and a Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “aa” (Superior), with a stable outlook. NSIC was included in the existing pooling agreement and parental guarantee alongside its three other US MS Transverse affiliates, adds the rating agency. MS Transverse Insurance Group is a property and casualty carrier and a subsidiary of Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance Group, and part of MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings (MS&AD).

item.title: Ageas Re continued to grow its 3rd Party Business in 2026 despite deteriorating market conditions
item.description: During the period, the reinsurer continued to grow its 3rd Party Business portfolio and also further strengthened the diversification of its underwriting platform, despite what the firm describes as a faster-than-expected deterioration in market conditions. This helped offset part of the market- driven rate reductions and demonstrated the continued confidence of clients and brokers in Ageas Re’s underwriting expertise, technical capabilities and long-term commitment.” Excluding Partnerships, total 3rd Party Business inflows increased by 38% year-on-year, with overall expected profitability modestly below the previous year as a result of market softening and mix of business effect due to deliberate increase in proportional business. Ageas Re, the reinsurance division of international insurance group Ageas, delivered strong growth in 3rd Party Business during its January-July 2026 renewal campaign, driven by increased shares on selected programmes and substantial new business generation.

item.title: Record-Low Danube Water Levels Leave Boats Beached, Reveal Decades-Old Shipwrecks
item.description: Danube levels fell to record lows this week in Croatia and Serbia, exposing hundreds of square kilometers of sand banks, following the summer’s prolonged heatwaves and drought that have affected waterways across Europe. Serbia’s fuel imports fell to 25% of their monthly target for July as low Danube water levels forced barges and tankers to operate at 30% to 40% of their cargo capacity, Energy Minister Dubravka Djedovic Handanovic said on Wednesday. In Serbia, low water levels in the Danube and the navigable rivers Tisa and Sava also hampered fisheries and tourism, while experts warned of long-term effects on wildlife.

item.title: Abbott Defeats Shareholder Lawsuit Over 2022 Infant Formula Recall
item.description: A federal judge on July 24 dismissed a lawsuit accusing Abbott Laboratories of defrauding shareholders by downplaying and trying to evade its responsibility for a 2022 recall of powdered infant formula, and lying about its commitment to quality and product safety. District Judge Steven Seeger in Chicago said shareholders led by two European asset managers failed to show that Abbott intended to deceive them and inflated its share price in connection with the February 2022 recall of Similac, Alimentum and EleCare produced at its plant in Sturgis, Michigan. The recall and plant closure worsened a national shortage of baby formula that began during the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Prompt Lawsuit From Small Businesses
item.description: Small businesses filed a pair of lawsuits in the US Court of International Trade accusing President Donald Trump and US officials of unlawfully using Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 to replace earlier tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court. The Trump administration is facing a fresh legal challenge to the president’s latest round of global tariffs that took effect Friday. Trump subsequently imposed 10% global tariffs, under Section 122 of the Trade Act, and those were ruled illegal by a trade court but were allowed to stay in effect during an appeal.

item.title: Travelers remains open to M&A following strong Q2
item.description: During the company’s July 17 earnings call, Chairman and CEO Alan Schnitzer said Travelers remains interested in strategic acquisitions and would be able to finance an attractive opportunity. Travelers reported $2.2 billion in second-quarter core income, or $10.04 per diluted share, as underwriting gains and higher investment income contributed to a core return on equity of 24.9%. Travelers’ most recent acquisition was cyber insurer Corvus Insurance, purchased for approximately $435 million in November 2023.

item.title: Vitality launches health podcast series
item.description: Vitality has launched The Good Health Edit , a health and wellness podcast hosted by clinical ambassador, GP and broadcaster Dr. Vitality said the series is intended to counter health misinformation and encourage people to take preventive action. The YouTube-exclusive series will combine expert commentary, personal experiences and practical advice covering topics including women’s health, parenting, nutrition, stress and emotional wellbeing.

item.title: Velocity Credit Union expands insurance offering
item.description: Velocity Credit Union has partnered with Inszone Insurance Services to give members access to personal, commercial, life, and pet insurance. “By partnering with Inszone Insurance Services, we’re giving members convenient access to experienced professionals who can help them find coverage that fits their lives today and adapts as their needs change.” – Debbie Mitchell, president and CEO of Velocity Credit Union. The Texas credit union is also offering hospital accident protection and recuperative care coverage through Allied Solutions and Franklin Madison Group.

item.title: Chubb launches embedded device insurance with Amazon
item.description: Chubb has partnered with Amazon to offer embedded device protection to customers in the UK and Spain. Amazon customers purchasing computers, tablets, and gaming devices can add coverage at the point of sale. The protection is integrated directly into Amazon’s shopping experience.

item.title: Navacord partners with Steers Insurance
item.description: Canadian insurance brokerage Navacord has partnered with Steers Insurance, expanding into Newfoundland and Labrador and establishing a coast-to-coast presence across Canada. Steers is the largest independent insurance brokerage in Newfoundland and Labrador, with eight locations, more than 100 employees and over C$110 million in gross written premium. As part of the transaction, several Steers employees will become Navacord shareholders.

item.title: Zurich Municipal launches insurance for England’s shadow authorities
item.description: Zurich Municipal has launched an insurance product for the temporary bodies overseeing England’s local government reorganization. Preparations will be managed by shadow authorities, which are legally separate from the existing councils and therefore require their own insurance. Zurich’s Shadow Authority Insurance includes property, business interruption, employers’ liability, public liability, officials’ indemnity, and libel and slander coverage.

item.title: MoneySuperMarket launches car insurance broker
item.description: MoneySuperMarket has partnered with insurance platform Open Insurance Technologies to launch a digital car insurance broker exclusively for its 2.5 million SuperSaveClub members. Bottom Line: The existing workflow sees MoneySuperMarket compare insurance from Allianz, Ford Insure, Britannia Car Insurance, Marshmallow , Skippy and Aviva. Members can compare, purchase, manage and renew policies without leaving MoneySuperMarket.

item.title: New York Approves 22% Workers’ Compensation Cost Reduction
item.description: New York has approved a 21.9% reduction in workers compensation insurance premium rates, which the state says represents an estimated savings of more than $1 billion for businesses or an average of $1,779 per employer in the state. The loss cost rate reduction was approved by the New York State Department of Financial Services (DFS) and will take effect on October 1, 2026. The latest reduction in insurance costs is in addition to a reduced employer assessment rate to cover the costs of the New York State Compensation Insurance Rating Board.

item.title: SpeedBuilder Launches FormMaker 2.0
item.description: (Image credit: IIR/Gemini.) SpeedBuilder Systems (Columbia, S.C.) has released FormMaker 2.0, the latest version of its insurance document automation solution for property/casualty insurers. FormMaker is integrated with Microsoft Word and SpeedBuilder’s BindExpress Suite, according to a company statement. SpeedBuilder says FormMaker 2.0 is intended to address the complexity of maintaining insurance forms, including frequent product updates, changing regulations and state-specific filing requirements.
